exposure: crash cesarean section indications (fetal bradycardia, prolapsed cord, uterine rupture, severe antepartum hemorrhage)
gestational age (<32 weeks, 32 to <37 weeks, >=37 weeks)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 103 women who underwent crash cesarean section at King Abdulaziz University hospital in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, between 2022 and 2023.
finding: Neonatal outcomes were better with shorter decision-to-delivery intervals (<=15 minutes) and in term deliveries compared to preterm deliveries.
mod_finding: Good neonatal outcome and lower respiratory distress syndrome were significantly associated with a decision-to-delivery interval of <=15 minutes in crash cesarean sections.
gest_age: Varied, including <32 weeks (16.7%), between 32 and <37 weeks (15.5%), and >=37 weeks (68.0%)
